_meta.description: Maps research events (seed/research/events.json) to data/event_types.json types. Every research event whose type is not in the vocabulary is mapped here; a few in-vocabulary events whose research shape contradicts design §5 are remapped too (ev024, ev030, ev054, ev067, ev085, ev098). Each research id maps to a list with one entry per effect; the seeder names them evNNNa, evNNNb, ... in list order. An empty list means no structural event (the research event is dropped; the reason is in 'notes').
_meta.keys: before/after use research keys. Excluded or held-out keys may appear; the seeder strips them and drops any entry left with empty before and after. Entries are written in the validator's shape: same-effect types list identical before and after; an absorption lists the absorber in both before and after.
_meta.unmapped_events: Research events not listed here keep their research type and shape. Note for the seeder: the research writes absorption as before=[absorbed], after=[absorber] and competence-transfer/attachment as before=[from], after=[to]; validator R4 needs the absorber in before too and identical before/after for same-effect types.
_meta.clauses: seed/clauses.json is keyed by research id; for an expanded event the clause belongs to the entry named in clauses.json _notes, otherwise to the first entry (ev024 -> ev024c, the suppression).
_meta.provenance: An entry may carry optional source_type and verified; they override the research event's provenance for that entry and may only downgrade it, never upgrade (tested). ev005's expansions are secondary/unverified because the list of the fifteen is secondary.

notes.ev028: Codex Iuris Canonici 1917 (in force 19 May 1918): no structural effect of its own. Its list of 11 congregations, 3 tribunals and 5 offices restates changes made by other acts with their own events (Seminaria clericorum ev026, Alloquentes proxime ev027, Dei providentis ev030). Its effect is the change of regime, recorded as cic-1917 in data/sections.json.
notes.ev118: Praedicate Evangelium as a whole: every structural effect the research found has its own event, so nothing is repeated here (repeating a merger would create a body twice): Minors placed within the DDF ev102, personal prelatures ev103, Evangelization merger ev104, Culture and Education merger ev105, Camera renamed ev106, renames to 'Dicasterium' ev107-ev117 (Almonry ev117). The abolition of PB bodies not provided for (Art. 250 §3) ends no research body without its own event. The change of regime is recorded as praedicate-evangelium-2022 in data/sections.json.
notes.ev120: General Regulation of the Roman Curia (signed 23 Nov 2025, known from a news report): no structural change reported, so no event.

ev005.note: Immensa aeterni Dei founds the Congregation for Sacred Rites and Ceremonies. The list of the fifteen Sixtine congregations and their titles is secondary (Catholic Encyclopedia); the act was not read; date and count verified from Sapienti consilio's recital.
Immensa founds the Congregation for the Erection of Churches and Consistorial Provisions (secondary list, as above).
Immensa founds the Congregation for Consultations of Bishops and other Prelates (secondary list, as above). H18: not the ancestor of the Congregation for Bishops.
Immensa founds the Congregation for the University of the Roman Study (secondary list, as above).
Immensa lists the Signatura gratiae among its fifteen (secondary). signatura-gratiae is HELD OUT (founding_years.json; identity open, ruling R11): the seeder strips it and drops this entry.
The six temporal congregations (one research placeholder). EXCLUDED in phase 1: the seeder strips the key and drops this entry.

ev022.note: Sapienti consilio creates the Congregation for the Discipline of the Sacraments (3rd congregation, 'new'); it takes sacramental/matrimonial matters from Council, Rites, Datary and Penitentiary (research erected.note). Other effects of the act have their own research events and are not repeated here: Inquisition renamed (ev021), Bishops-and-Regulars dissolved (ev024), Religious created (ev024), Lauretana united to Council (ev018), Revision of Councils ended (ev019), Visitation suppressed (ev025), Rota revived (ev023), Signatura re-founded (ev020). The Secretariat of Briefs becoming the 3rd part of the Secretariat of State is a placement between two held-out bodies and is omitted.

Research names[] change Rites' name at 1908-11-03 ('Congregatio pro sacris ritibus et caeremoniis' -> 'Sacra Congregatio Rituum') citing Sapienti consilio, with no event; the act uses the new name but the research quotes no renaming clause, hence inferred.

Holy Office loses ecclesiastical precepts (to Council), the election of bishops (to Consistorial) and dispensation of religious vows (to Religious) (research competence_changes of the Inquisition, primary, verified).

Holy Office gains all matters of indulgences (research competence_changes, primary). The research does not name the losing body; Rites is inferred because it had absorbed the Congregation of Indulgences and Relics in 1904 and 'in 1908 indulgences went to the Holy Office and relics to Rites' (research note on indulgences-relics).

ev024.note: The diocesan matters of Bishops-and-Regulars go to the Consistorial (Sapienti consilio 2° n.3, research ended.note, primary). A transfer to a body that keeps its key. The research's other stated transfer (religious matters to the new Congregation of Religious) is NOT encoded as an event: it would precede that body's foundation and would read as succession, and whether Religious continues the Regulars line is open (H8).

Sapienti consilio creates the Congregation of Religious as a new congregation (5th; research erected, primary). Recorded as a foundation, not as the product of a split: it is not made a successor of Bishops-and-Regulars (H8 stays an open question).

Suppression by omission, design §5 rule 8 (its worked example, H9): Bishops-and-Regulars is not named as suppressed; it is omitted from Sapienti consilio's closed list ('non alia sint ... quam quae praesenti Constitutione decernuntur'); research ended.how = 'suppressed'. Dated to the constitution's effective date, inferred. The research typed the whole event 'split' with consistorial-bishops and religious-consecrated-life in 'after'.

ev026.note: H11, Seminaria clericorum: the act founds a congregation for seminaries ('De Seminariis propria iam esto Sacra Congregatio'), adds the functions of the Congregation of Studies and gives the combined name; it never says Studies is suppressed. Reading A (rename of Studies, kept) vs reading B (new body absorbing Studies) are equally defensible; the research models continuity, so: rename, inferred (brief).

ev051.note: Research type 'rename+kind-change' mapped to 'rename' (brief); the kind change is carried by the body's dated kind list, not by the event. Congregation for Extraordinary Ecclesiastical Affairs becomes 'Sacrum Consilium pro Publicis Ecclesiae negotiis' (REU n.26); kind congregation -> council.

ev052.note: REU creates the Administration of the Patrimony of the Apostolic See (REU n.123; report §2 item 7 'New'). Event date 1968-01-01 (in force); the research erected.date 1967-08-15 is the signing date (see key_map founded_date). Other REU effects have their own research events: renames ev045-ev051, absorption of the Briefs offices ev044, suppression of Datary ev053 and Ceremonial ev054.
REU creates the Prefecture for the Economic Affairs of the Holy See (REU n.117). Same date note as APSA.

REU creates the Prefecture of the Apostolic Palace (REU n.125). Same date note as APSA. Ceremonial's non-liturgical ceremonies pass to it (REU n.126; partial, inferred succession in research), recorded in ev054's note, not as an absorption.

ev054.note: Ceremonial is not named in REU (suppression by omission, inferred: design §5 rule 8). The research put papal-household-prefecture in 'after'; a suppression has no 'after' (it ends a body). The non-liturgical ceremonies pass to the Prefecture of the Apostolic Palace (REU n.126) as a partial, inferred succession, kept here as a note only. Ceremonial is HELD OUT, so the seeder strips it and drops this event.

ev064.note: Research type 'rename+kind-change' mapped to 'rename' (brief); the kind change is carried by the body's dated kind list, not by the event. 1976: rename + permanent status + new internal order in one act (same pattern as CDF 1965, H1); 'in posterum appellabitur' (H17 contrast).

ev067.note: H15, Recognito Iuris Canonici Codice: the act 'erects' a new commission following Benedict XV's precedent, with no succession clause. Design §5 rule 6 treats succession by imitation as re-foundation (new key, linked as successor). The research typed it 'foundation' with the 1917 commission in 'before'. The end of the 1917 commission is inferred (research ended source_type inferred).

ev030.note: H12, Dei providentis: the old body 'esse desinat' on 30 Nov 1917 and a new congregation is set up 'seorsum' from Propaganda from 1 Dec 1917 — a clean end plus a new foundation. Remapped from the research 'split' (one successor only, the original does not divide). Re-foundation (design §5 rule 6) rather than suppression + foundation, so that the successor link the report traces (§3, Eastern Churches) is kept; the act states the cessation and the new body explicitly, but not a succession, hence inferred. Date note for the seeder: the research event date is 1917-11-30, oriental-churches' erected.date 1917-12-01.
